hook.text: During COVID, the U.S. sent $5 trillion in stimulus. People had money but factories were shut. Prices exploded.

buildup.text: Demand-pull inflation happens when too much money chases too few goods. Buyers compete and prices rise.

discovery.text: Milton Friedman said it simply: inflation is always a monetary phenomenon. More money, higher prices.

twist.text: But not always. Japan printed trillions and had near-zero inflation for 30 years. Money alone isn't enough.

climax.text: Demand-pull inflation requires both excess money and willingness to spend it. Psychology matters as much as supply.

quiz.question: What causes demand-pull inflation?
options: Too much money chasing too few goods
